The wheel is said to be of five kinds; therein one should worship the Power (*śakti*). The Royal Wheel (*rājacakra*), the Great Wheel (*mahācakra*), the Divine Wheel (*devacakra*) as the third, and the Heroic Wheel (*vīracakra*) as the fourth.

And the Paśucakra is the fifth. O Kulasundarī! A Vīra should worship within the five divine cakras; both the celibate student (brahmacārī) and the householder (gṛhastha) should perform worship in the five cakras. O Queen of the Gods! One who is more powerful should perform worship in the Śivacakra; the celibate student and the householder should worship by means of the Vīracakra.

O Goddess! In the previous cakras, the Kāminī is worshipped by yogins. One should worship these five in the Rājacakra: the mother, the sister, the daughter, the daughter-in-law, and likewise the wife of the guru.
O Mistress of the Kula! Wine made from molasses (gauḍī) or from honey (mādhvī) is recommended.

The urine of a pure goat is recommended, as is the third [type], that from the *uddālaka* plant. Mudrā made from wheat is recommended, as is the *svayambhū* flower. One should employ substances produced from the *kuṇḍa* and *goḷa* as secondary alternatives (*anukalpa*). Likewise, red sandalwood and white sandalwood are also secondary alternatives.
With sandalwood, garments, ornaments, decorations, perfumes, garlands, and ointments,
one should worship with supreme devotion and offer [these] to the deities. One should also offer various kinds of edible substances, accompanied by diverse garments, and a seat.
One should repeatedly offer [the oblation] to them while joined with purity; having prostrated and beheld them, one should recite the mantra one thousand times. One must not touch their limbs;
if one touches them, one shall go to hell. When they are intoxicated by honey...

Those with great prosperity sleep [in peace]. All this shall indeed be so; it is the truth, the truth, there is no doubt. For sixty thousand years, one is glorified in the world of Brahmā. O Mistress of the Clan! One should worship these—the mother, the sister, the daughter-in-law, the maiden, and the wife of a hero—in the Great Wheel (Mahācakra).

The five powers (pañcaśakti) should be worshipped again and again when giving material substances; however, one should not perform the union with Śiva while lacking those powers. If one performs the union without power, there will be a loss of accomplishment (siddhi), and one shall go to the Raurava hell. O Goddess! A great disease shall arise, and the loss of wealth occurs constantly.

He incurs suffering and everything belonging to him perishes. The first is said to be from *gauḍika*, the second is produced from a cock, the third is said to be *rohita*, and the fourth arises from a hare.
[The fifth is] the flower produced from the *karavīra* and sandalwood.

One should worship with supreme devotion using red sandalwood; one is glorified in the world of Śiva. For sixty thousand years, one shall worship the Goddess there on the eighth, the fourteenth, and the new moon day, as well as on Tuesdays, with devotion during the Rājacakras and Mahācakras.

One should worship Śakti. On a Thursday during the bright fortnight, on the fourth or seventh lunar day, one should worship with devotion in the Great Wheel for the sake of accomplishing all desires and aims. O lady of excellent complexion, listen as I describe the Devacakra; it is known by the wise of all castes.

One should worship five maidens. The first is made of molasses, which is delightful and fruit-bestowing; the second is derived from birds; the third is the *śālamatsya*; the fourth is derived from grains. One should employ fragrant flowers of all kinds in the circle of the deities (*devacakra*). In the circle of the deities, one should worship Śakti.
One is glorified in the circle of the gods for sixty thousand years; one should worship the divine maiden in the circle.

One should worship five maidens in the circle, never more than that. O lady of excellent complexion! If there should be union with them through greed, desire, or even deception, [one goes] to the Raurava hell.
On the eighth and fourteenth days of both fortnights, having gone to the abode of the ancestors,
the practitioner of mantra, accompanied by divine heroes, should worship within the *vīracakra* and honor the most powerful Śakti.
The Goddess said:
O Lord, how is it that the five maidens, beginning with Mātrā, belong to the ascetics?
The illustrious Śiva said:
O Dear One! Since the five maidens beginning with Mātrā were born of low castes—the courtesan originating from the four varṇas being especially powerful;
the daughter of the lord of the earth was the mother; the daughter of the washerman was the daughter; and the daughter of the outcaste was the sister.

The Kāpālī is known as the daughter-in-law; the Yoginī is one's own power (śakti). These are proclaimed as the five maidens. This should be performed in the presence of the Guru or together with one's brothers. A hero becomes one whose mantra is perfected, not by the drinking of wine.

The hero shall be consecrated, and the Kaulikī [goddess] shall be consecrated. In this manner, one should employ the Hero and the Śakti within the Vīracakra. Furthermore, there is the secret convention of the sequence (*krama-saṅketaka*), as well as the secret convention of worship (*pūjā-saṅketaka*), the secret convention of mantra (*mantra-saṅketaka*), and likewise the secret convention of the yantra (*yantra-saṅketaka*). [This is] the writing.

The convention of mantras and yantras [is obtained] from the path of the Guru. O Goddess, if one should employ a hero in the wheel without that which is born of convention, the worship is fruitless; for him there is suffering at every step.
That hero who is devoid of convention and has not been consecrated through the lineage of the Gurus is like one who has fallen into a well.

That most wicked man shall abandon him in the circle of heroes (vīracakra). Having seated one who is not consecrated in the left circle, or a Kaulika woman who is not consecrated, he goes to the Raurava hell; this is the truth, the truth, there is no doubt. O Goddess, if one should dwell in the circle of heroes without such a sequence, [he likewise falls].

There is a loss of accomplishment; through the loss of accomplishment, one goes to the Raurava hell. O Kuleśvarī! [One should offer] all liquor, all pure substances, all fish, all mudrās, all flowers, as well as the self-arisen flower (svayambhūkusuma) and the substance produced from the *kuṇḍa* and *golaka*.
The best of practitioners should repeatedly offer food endowed with various flavors into the *vīracakra*.
There, he should worship his own consort (*śakti*) and drink her leavings, O Dear One!
He should take the chewable food from his elder and present it to the younger; he should not eat while sitting on the same seat [as another].

One should not eat from a single vessel, nor should one ever touch one another. O Goddess of the Gods! One should proceed in this manner within the *vīracakra*. Having brought a woman of low birth as a goddess, one should purify her with the *śakti-mantra*. Having thus purified the woman of low birth...

One should present the goddess, the heroic power (vīraśakti). He who gives a beautiful woman of low birth to a hero intoxicated by honey [wine] performs the gift of power to the hero; this is ordained in the Vīracakra.
If the circle is broken, one should perform the gift [of penance]; otherwise, one shall go to the Raurava hell.

One should destroy or conceal [these], but never criticize or look upon them; likewise, one should conceal lust, anger, envy, transformation, greed, family scandal, foul speech, and wickedness, O Beloved! [One should also conceal] the mantra, the mudrā, the rosary, and the yoni.
One should conceal the assembly of heroes, the mandala, the jar, the seat, and the perfected substances.

One should not, even in thought, revile the wise one, the lineage of heroes, the field, the goddess Yoginī, the teacher of the Kula conduct, or the messenger (dūtī). [One should honor] the goddess, the teacher, and the nectar.

One should worship the supreme Vidyā, Śakti born of Kriyā, the Yoginī, the essence of Bhairavī, and the essence of the Self (Ātmatattva). In the wheel of the bound souls (Paśucakra), the wise one should worship the stepmother, the daughter, the sister, the daughter-in-law, and the wife as the fifth; he should act to please them like a bound soul.
O beautiful one! O beloved! [Offer] perfumes, flowers, garlands, garments, and ornaments;
vermilion, agallochum, musk, and various blossoms;
diverse kinds of edible substances and various fruits.

Whoever should offer this collection of substances to those two with devotion will certainly become a king upon the earth for sixty thousand years; then, in the Vīracakra, accomplishment (siddhi) is attained without a doubt.
Now, the Kula Śaktis. In the third chapter of the *Revatītantra*:

"O Supreme Goddess! All women are Śaktis who are wise [in this regard]: the actress (*naṭī*), the Kāpālikī, the courtesan (*veśyā*), Mālinī, Kuṅkumālinī, the Caṇḍālī, the potter-woman (*kulālī*), the washerwoman (*rajakī*), the barber’s wife (*nāpitāṅganā*), and the cowherd’s wife (*gopinī*)."

The Yoginī, the pure Brāhmaṇī, the princess, the Kocā woman, O Mistress of the Gods! and likewise the Śaṅkhakāriṇī—these twenty-six maidens are difficult even for the gods to obtain. Also the Daivajñā, the Vyādhavāmā, and the Māṃsāpahāriṇī.
O Goddess! The Bauddhā, the Yavanī, the Rasapasāriṇī, and the Veśyā are declared to be the four types;
the Kuṅkumālinī is of two kinds; the Dhīvarī is said to be of two kinds, as is the Gaṇikāṅganā; the Kumbhakārī is said to be of two kinds, and the Gopinī is likewise remembered as being of two kinds.

O Goddess! The Vātavaidyā woman is remembered as being of two kinds, O Devi! The Bauddhakanyā is of three kinds, O Devi! And likewise, O Beloved, the Kocā woman [is of one kind]; together with those previously mentioned, there are sixty-four Śaktis in all.
In the fourth chapter of the Guptasādhanatantra.
Śiva said:

Listen, Pārvatī! I shall declare this great and most profound secret. Through its disclosure, there would be a loss of spiritual accomplishment; therefore, one should guard it with great effort. [One should choose] a woman who is either one's own power (*svaśakti*) or another's power (*paraśakti*), who has been initiated, endowed with youth, clever, beautiful, and pure.
"Having brought one who is devoid of compassion and shame, he should perform the *kulasādhana*";

this is the connection with the following [verse]. Regarding that, he states the established rule in the eighth chapter of the *Niruttaratantra*: "Having obtained the accomplishment of his own *śakti*, he then becomes one whose mantra is perfected."

One who has mastered the mantra should worship the wives of others according to the Kula practice. One who has mastered the mantra should worship Śakti with body or even with mind; especially the wives of others—one should worship the wives of others. The method for mastering the mantra is in the ninth chapter. And having brought the Kula...

O Goddess! One should then write the beautiful *kula-śakti* for the *kulārcana*, as well as one's own various *cakra*s upon the forehead of the *śakti*. Thereafter, one should write the Goddess Kāmakalā in the corner of the hero (*vīra*). In the center of that, one should place the prescribed mantra of the deity, marked with the sign of desire (*kāma*). Therein is the Goddess.

Having invoked [the deity] and meditated upon him, one should worship him; then, with a steady mind, the Kula practitioner should perform a hundred thousand recitations (*japa*). Then, he should whisper the root mantra three times into the ear of that [deity's] Śakti, accompanied by the names of the *ṛṣi* and the *chandas*.

[The Guru says] into her left ear: "From this day forward, O Śakti, perform the worship of the Kula deity! Then the Śakti recites: "Having received the command of the Guru, free from pity and shame, O Lord, I shall perform the Kula worship according to the rite spoken by Śiva. Protect me, O Nātha!"

O Leader of those who desire the conduct of their own clan! Grant me the shade of your lotus feet upon the path of the clan. When the first watch of the night has passed, having brought [the consort] adorned in red garments to your left side, place her above the head of the clan.
Having written the mantra on the forehead, adorned with various perfumes and endowed with various jewels, with the name inscribed in the center;
having filled the mouth with betel and having eyes reddened by betel, one should perform the recitation of the *kula* and *akula*.

It certainly arrives at that very moment. When the mantra has been thus drawn forth, O Kuleśvarī, one who possesses a perfected mantra (siddhamantra) should perform the practice for as long as success (siddhi) does not arise.
One who possesses a perfected mantra should worship the women of the Kula according to the Kula tradition within the limbs of Śakti. [End of] Śaktyaṅga.

He states the place for recitation (*japa*) in the *Samayācāra-tantra*: "Now I shall proclaim the supreme seat (*pīṭha*) for the purpose of recitation: Pūrṇagiri is the first, Uḍḍiyāna the second, Jālandhara the third, and Kāmarūpa the fourth. In the Kṛta [Yuga]...

Pūrṇagiri is the second [seat] in the Tretā age; Jālandhara in the Dvāpara age, and Kāmarūpa in the Kali age. I shall describe those four seats which are the most secret of secrets, the seats that reside within the bodies of Śakti—the entire body of Śakti.
That seat which is known as Pūrṇagiri is her head, O fortunate one!
Uḍḍīyāna is proclaimed to be [her] neck; Jālandhara should be known as her breasts, and Kāmarūpa likewise as her vulva.
Among all these, the seat of desire (Kāmapīṭha) is difficult even for the gods to attain. In these...

O Dear One! By remaining upon the sacred seats (pīṭhas) and reciting whichever mantra one may, one obtains that very fruit, and the deity quickly becomes propitious. Likewise, O Fortunate One, those practitioners who engage in conversation with the various Śaktis attain success in a short time.

Human beings shall attain the fruit. Having brought her, the lord of practitioners should offer auspicious water for the feet and other honors. Having worshipped that Śakti according to the rule with the fivefold conduct (pañcācāra), [he should offer] a hundred [prostrations] on the head, a hundred on the forehead, and a hundred...
On the circle of vermilion (sindūra), one hundred [times]; on the face, one hundred; on the throat, one hundred; on the circle of the heart, one hundred;

on the pair of breasts, two hundred; on the navel, one hundred—the wise practitioner should recite thus. Having recited one hundred times on the seat of the womb (yonipīṭha), the practitioner of steady mind, having thus recited one thousand times—

The best of practitioners should meditate on her as having the form of a goddess; he should meditate on her as being the very nature of Śiva and Śakti. Then, O Goddess of the gods, he should worship his own *liṅga* with the Śiva-mantra.
Having placed betel-leaf in her mouth, the practitioner, with a joyful mind, [should seek] her permission.

Having taken up the *liṅga*, one should cast it into the source (*yoni*). With this mantra—"Oṃ! In the fire of the Self, kindled by the oblation of dharma and adharma, I constantly offer the functions of the senses with the mind as the ladle, through the path of the *suṣumṇā*—Svāhā!"—one should perform the oblation.
For the sake of all prosperity, one should then recite [the mantra] a thousand times; indeed, the person shall become endowed with power.
Or else, it should be recited a hundred times; one should not perform less than that. Then the practitioner should offer the final oblation (pūrṇāhuti) with this mantra.

Supporting [the ladle] with the hands of light and space, being in the state of *unmanā*, I offer into the fire that which is filled with the oil of the portions of merit and demerit by means of the *sruc* ladle.
One should perform the final oblation (*pūrṇāhuti*) with this mantra: "Svāhā! At the time of the emission of the semen, however, [it is offered] to Mahādevī.

One should offer [the oblation]. When this is done, the accomplishment of the mantra (*mantrasiddhi*) certainly occurs; there is no doubt. Whatever desire one prays for, that one will surely attain. A sick person shall be freed from disease, and a lord of wealth shall become rich. Possessing strength equal to the wind in this world, he shall be invincible and a crusher of enemies.

Equal to Kāma among women and like a destroyer of enemies, O Goddess of gods! what on this earth cannot be accomplished by this ritual? He alone attains the eightfold sovereign powers; he indeed is Śrī Sadāśiva himself.

Also, in the twelfth chapter of the *Niruttaratantra*: "Now I shall further explain a means of accomplishment (*sādhana*) difficult to find on earth; by performing which one obtains a success (*siddhi*) that is difficult even for the gods to attain. A wise person should write the mantra of Śakti on the forehead, repeating it three times."

In the center of that, one should draw the seed-syllable of Kāma, marked with the emblem of Kāma; having encased it within Kāma, one should worship the Supreme Goddess. Having fully worshipped the goddess Kālikā, one should worship the yantra as well. Intent on the contemplation of reality, the yogi should recite the mantra one hundred thousand times without distraction.

Having gathered the *kulapuṣpa* flowers, one should worship them again and again; one should satisfy [the deity] a thousand times on the seat with the water used for washing the *yantra*. When this is done, one shall obtain success—this is the truth, the truth, there is no doubt. Now I shall explain another matter.

This is the supreme *puraścaraṇa*: one hundred [offerings] on the forehead, one hundred in the hair, one hundred in the circle of vermilion (*sindūra*); one hundred on the lotus-face, two hundred on the flower-like face;
two hundred on the pair of breasts, and one hundred in the circle of the navel; one hundred—
One should recite [the mantra] with a spirit of devotion in the family shrine (*kulāgāra*). Having thus recited it one thousand times, one should then recite it in the family shrine;

having performed worship, one should recite the mantra one thousand times, ending with the word "Gaja" (elephant). Then, through the yoga of reality (*tattva*), one should recite it one hundred and eight times. Thereafter, the worship is to be performed there.

The preliminary rite (puraścaraṇa) is now described. Furthermore, O Mistress of the Kula! I shall explain another method for the accomplishment of the Kula-abode, by performing which all sins are destroyed. In the Kula-abode, on the eighth day of the Kula-month, one should summon the Kula and perform worship, libation (tarpaṇa), recitation (japa), and fire-offering (homa).

That [offering] shall become inexhaustible. And if the root of a plantain tree is seen to be double [in size], then, O lady of excellent complexion, a great worship must be performed there! Thereafter, the wise man should perform the fire-oblation (homa) with the mouth of Brahmā; having performed the oblation, he should recite the mantra.

It shall become ten million times ten millionfold in merit. He who, having gazed upon the root of the *rajanī* plant, recites the mantra twice over, shall become the lord of all supernatural powers (*siddhis*); his merit cannot be calculated.
Having summoned the *rajanī* at will, this practice, which is the ornament of the *kula*, is performed in reverse.

The merit of one who chants the mantra for him cannot be calculated. If one is skilled in worship during the night in the house of the lineage (kulāgāra), then she who is like you—whether it be Rājanīkāntā, Kamalā, or Rādhikā—is blessed in the three worlds as the essence of Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Śiva; she is the perfected knowledge (siddhavidyā).
The Great Vidyā is the bestower of the fruits of perfected knowledge; by her mere grace, even a wicked mantra becomes effective. Therefore, with every effort, one should seek refuge in her alone.
If the practitioner should practice the Rajanī-yoga at night, whether by force or otherwise—

Whatever one worships there shall become fruitless. By whatever means possible—whether through external acts, through play, or even through subjugation—one should always satisfy her. Whatever state of being belongs to the Night (Rajanī), that very state [one should assume].

One should perform the ritual arrangement. If one acts with excess, that state leads to the Raurava hell. Having obtained the consent of the *kalā*, one should accomplish the *kula*-sādhana. From association with a *kula* without consent, the loss of accomplishment (*siddhi*) arises. He who goes to the house of the Night (the consort) devoid of the *kula*-sādhana—[he...]
Thus one goes to hell; this is the truth, the truth, there is no doubt. Whether out of anger, desire, or hatred, O fair-complexioned lady! one should not go to the house during the night;
if one should enter the Kula-path without knowing the Kula-convention, he [goes to hell].
He goes to a terrible hell; what need is there to speak of his future birth?

Now, the purification of the bed: *Oṃ āḥ surekhe vajrarekhe hūṃ phaṭ svāhā*. Having drawn a triangle on the bed with this mantra, one should worship it mentally with: *Oṃ hrīṃ ādhāraśaktaye kamalāsanāya namaḥ*. Then, *Oṃ hrīṃ*...

Having struck the corpse three times with the left hand while reciting the mantra *mṛtakāya namaḥ phaṭ*, and having performed the binding of the ten directions with snapping sounds (*choṭikā*), one should say: "O Śayyā! You are the form of the deceased;
you are to be accomplished by practitioners. Therefore, the mantra is being recited here for our sake."
"Be the bestower of success. Having made this prayer, one should perform the recitation (*japa*) and other rites.

In the first chapter of the *Guptasādhanatantra*: "O Goddess, one should worship the Kula-śakti through the fivefold conduct (*pañcācāra*). [These are: the dancer, the Kāpālikī, the courtesan, the washerwoman, the barber’s wife, the Brāhmaṇī, the Śūdra girl, likewise the cowherd’s daughter, and the florist’s [daughter]."

The maiden and the nine maidens are thus proclaimed; all of them are noble women endowed with exceptional skill, possessed of beauty and youth, and distinguished by virtue and good fortune. They should be worshipped with diligent effort, for from that, success will certainly arise.
Regarding this, it is specified in the fourteenth chapter of the *Niruttara Tantra*: "The Naṭī, the Kāpālikī, the Veśyā, the Rajakī, the Nāpitāṅganā, the Yoginī, the Śvapacī, the Śuṇḍī,
likewise the Bhūmīndratanayā, the Gopinī of the florist— of these..."

(1069) Due to the distinction of her function, she who arises from the four castes and is beautiful is proclaimed as the Kāpālī. Having observed the materials for worship, she who desires sexual union is the one who arises from the four castes and is beautiful; she is proclaimed as the Veśyā. [The materials for worship...]
She who, having looked all around and inspected the articles of worship,

reveals her royal status, and who is beautiful and born from any caste, is proclaimed as the *Rajakī*. Having inspected the articles of worship, she who is of noble birth (*kulajā*) abandons [her former state] and takes refuge with the hero.

A woman who serves her husband as a slave is known as a *karmacāṇḍālinī*. She who takes delight in inverted sexual union (*viparītarata*) with her husband and asks for a vessel [to hold his semen] is proclaimed as a beautiful *śauṇḍī*, regardless of the caste from which she is born. She in whom the refinement of the *yantra* (the female organ) is constantly produced is indeed...

O Beloved! She who is born from a solar complexion, beautiful as the earth-lord’s daughter, and who always protects herself amidst the throngs of common folk, she who is beautiful and born of all castes is proclaimed as Gopinī. She who, upon beholding the materials for worship, becomes as delighted as if she were wearing a garland—she is Gopinī.
That Mālinī is proclaimed as beautiful, arising from all the castes.

The specific distinctions regarding the *veśyā* are stated in that very same source: "The *guptaveśyā*, the *mahāveśyā*, the *kulaveśyā*, the *mahodayā*, the *rājaveśyā*, the *devaveśyā*, and the *brahmaveśyā*—thus she is sevenfold. The *guptaveśyā* is one born of noble family (*kulajā*), who is shameless and afflicted by passion."

In this world, one who depends on a husband is proclaimed as a "hidden courtesan" (*guptaveśyā*). One born of a noble family is a "family courtesan" (*kulaveśyā*), while one who is highly renowned is proclaimed a "great courtesan" (*mahāveśyā*). She should repeatedly kiss the sacred seat (*pīṭha*) of the vulva and the phallus;
if she is of such a nature and of noble lineage, she is proclaimed a "Brahma-courtesan" (*brahmaveśyā*).
Divya-śakti and Vīra-śakti are proclaimed as their designations;
these designations are defined for those born from the four castes (*varṇa*).
Because she wanders like a courtesan (*veśyā*), she is therefore proclaimed a *veśyā*. [This occurs] due to the mixture of castes (*varṇasaṅkara*).

She who is born [into this state] is proclaimed as a universal courtesan (*sarvaveśyā*). She who is engaged in the path of the lineage (*kulamārga*) is a courtesan who bestows liberation. Kissing, embracing, striking, witnessing the restraint in lovemaking, addressing her at the three junctions of the day, and the recitation of the names of the vulva and the phallus—these belong to the courtesans.

This was previously declared by Śaṅkara as an auxiliary to the *japa*: "In the worship of a noble family, a prostitute must be avoided unless she performs the auxiliary *japa*. She should perform the auxiliary *japa* every day and rejoice together with the Śivas.
At night, she should recite the mantra through union with Svayambhū-Śiva. [Regarding] prostitutes...

(1070) Merely reciting [the mantra] is called *puraścaraṇa*. One should recite the mantra in reverse; she is Kālī, of this there is no doubt. O Dear One! For women, the accomplishment of the mantra occurs during reverse sexual union (*viparītarati*). Having recited it during reverse sexual union, one shall go to the state of Nirvāṇa. During reverse sexual union...
Having performed the recitation, one should wander upon the earth like Kālī. In inverted sexual union (*viparītarati*), Kālī is inverted, and Tāriṇī is also inverted;

she who is the inverted prostitute is Kālī—of this there is no doubt. Without inverted sexual union, the sciences (*vidyās*) of women do not succeed. The prostitute who delights in inverted union is worshiped throughout the three worlds.

Having given a firm embrace and having worshipped her again and again, one should show the yantra with side-long glances; this is called the *dakṣiṇākālī* [rite]. O Mistress of the Kula! Such is the preliminary practice (*puraścaryā*) for a prostitute. A prostitute should be of such a nature, and not otherwise.

O beloved! A prostitute (*veśyā*) is an unchaste woman (*kulaṭā*). By associating with an unchaste woman, one goes to the Raurava hell. However, a prostitute who possesses heroic power (*vīraśakti*) is recommended for the practice of the *kula* tradition. A prostitute who has performed the preliminary rites (*puraścaryā*) may be employed in the *kula* practice. She is virtuous when she is united with the Śiva-linga; she is virtuous when she is united with the Śiva-linga.
A prostitute who has taken refuge in the Śiva-linga is proclaimed to be a devoted wife (pativratā).

The womb is the mother who gives birth, and the linga is the father who begets. One should contemplate the state of both as mother and father: Mahākāla is the form of the linga, and Kālikā is the form of the womb; she is intent on their union.

Blessed is that great one who is intent on their union. He who performs the worship of Śiva without his own Bhairava [consort] shall dwell in the terrible Raurava hell until the dissolution of all beings. A hero should not mentally recall another woman apart from his own Bhairavī; by such recollection, he goes to hell.

She would become afflicted by a great disease. A courtesan who resorts to various practices and who has entered into union with common cattle (or lowly men) must be avoided with effort in the ritual practice (*sādhana*) of the *kula*. If she were employed [in such rites], there would be a loss of accomplishment (*siddhi*).
Even in the worship of the *kula*, an excellent courtesan [should be used]; otherwise, illness, grief, and the loss of wealth will befall her.
Moment by moment. Therefore, with every effort, one should take refuge in one’s own Śiva.

A courtesan should perform recitation, worship, and other rites for her own Śiva. A courtesan who is in full bloom, possessed of desire, and always longing for dalliance, is Kālikā, the bestower of all accomplishments.

She who bears form is proclaimed as the ancestral ground (*pitṛbhūmi*), the dwelling place of Sadāśiva. Since man is to be known as Śiva himself, bearing the form of the *liṅga*, the cremation ground (*śmaśāna*) is the abode of Śiva; the cremation ground is the Guru born of the *kula*. And on the eighth day... [p. 1071]

On the fourteenth day of both fortnights, whatever task is performed by one staying in a cremation ground must necessarily be weighty. Likewise: Having offered the eternal [oblation] into the mouth of the Mother, one should recite [the mantra] into the mouth of the Father; thus liberated from all sins, one shall go to the state of Nirvāṇa.

In a future birth, she may become either a secret courtesan or one born of noble family; know, O Pārvatī, that liberation occurs at the time of the emission of semen. For at that moment, Mahākāla is present for those who have entered the path of the Kula. One should recognize the time of the emission of semen even by means of the mind.

One should reveal [the teaching] to a person of noble lineage (kulīna) through the sequence of the breaking of the limbs; for by making known the time of the emission of semen, Kālikā herself [is pleased]. Regarding the limb of recitation: "O Goddess Kālikā! You shall utterly delude Mahākāla. If she is a noble Brahmin-prostitute (brahmaveśyā), then it is not the fruit of meager austerity.

At the end of many births, one is born as a Brahmin courtesan; yet, even if there were someone on the circle of the earth whose nature was equal to yours, no power equal to yours exists within the three worlds. She herself is Dakṣiṇā Kālī, overwhelmed and agitated by the god of love, and she is born from the Vedas.

Bondage arises from action through action. Having completely renounced Vedic ritual, one should always mutter [mantras] during sexual union. Śambhu is the Lord taught in the Āgamas; the Guru is the Lord taught in the Āgamas. He is the Lord of the woman born of the Kula, and not the husband married by worldly rite. There is no fault in abandoning a husband who has been married by worldly rite.

In the worship of the Kula, one must never abandon the married husband during the performance of Vedic rites. However, the husband prescribed by the Āgamas is the protector, and the husband prescribed by the Āgamas is Śiva. Without the husband prescribed by the Āgamas, the accomplished vidyās do not attain success. O Goddess! One born of the Kula should perform the formal selection (*varaṇa*) of the Guru as the husband; then [success follows].

She may be a guarded courtesan (*guptaveśyā*) or one born of noble family (*kulajā*), yet devoid of a husband; she alone shall be a guarded courtesan who sets the path of the *kula* in motion. She who has entered the path of the *kula* is liberated—of this there is no doubt. O Goddess, if a woman born of noble family does not desire a husband for the sake of her Guru, Śiva [is pleased] with her.
Mahākāla is the truth, the truth; there is no doubt. When she is sixteen years old, she is Kālī, intent on valor; at fifteen, Tārā;
at fourteen, Sundarī; and at thirteen, she is Unmukhī.
And Bhairavī is twelve years of age; endowed with eleven qualities, O Kuleśvarī, she is the courtesan of Brahmā. She is celebrated as a great chaste woman, difficult to find in the three worlds.
She is the mistress of all those women who abide in heaven, on earth, and in the netherworld.

The practitioner is divine and heroic. When the divine one becomes a hero, he shall become the lord of all women. Even the divine one, through the state of a hero, should worship those born of every caste. O Dear One! [These are] the secret courtesans, the great courtesans, Ayodhyā, and Mathurā; and whosoever are the family courtesans.

Madodagrā and Kālikā may also be [there]. Dvārakā is proclaimed as both a royal courtesan (rājaveśyā) and a divine courtesan (devaveśyā). Kāñcī is a royal courtesan, while Avantikā is indeed a divine courtesan.
Dvārāvatī is a brahmin courtesan; these hidden ones are the bestowers of liberation. The Blessed Lady is of noble lineage.
Kālī, Tārā, and Sarasvatī are manifest; Bhairavī is manifest as Kulīnā; Sundarī is the goddess Kulīnā;
Mahiṣamardinī is Kulīnā;
Bhuvanā, Bālā, and Vagalāmukhī are Kulīnā; and Dhūmāvatī is also Kulīnā.

Mātaṅgī is the mistress of the Kula! Annapūrṇā is of noble lineage, and Tvaritā is likewise of noble lineage. The devoted wife is of noble lineage; she is a virtuous, chaste woman of great prosperity. She is of noble lineage, the bestower of success in mantras and yantras—of this there is no doubt. She is born of noble family and is a daughter of the gods.
The hosts of yoginīs are of noble birth; Rambhā, Urvaśī, Ratī, Rāmā, and Tilottamā are likewise of noble lineage.

All these, though distinct as courtesans, sport as daughters of noble families. She who is born of a noble family, who is a noble courtesan, and who is devoted to the dharma of her family, yet remains fickle and dependent upon a worldly master.

One who is languid with desire and curiosity, always eager for dalliance according to the traditional path of the family, and intent on concealing her heroism through the demeanor of a clever woman— such a woman should be appointed as the low-born consort (*hīnajā*),
whom one should then worship while restraining one's speech. Even a celibate student (*brahmacārī*) or a householder (*gṛhastha*) should not [approach] another woman [thus ordained].

And one should worship her. If she is not worshipped, there will be a loss of accomplishment and suffering at every step. One should mentally worship a prostitute of low birth who has been ordained for this purpose. The wise one should contemplate union with her and recite the mantra one hundred and eight times. Having recited it and bowed, O Goddess of Gods, [one should offer] edible substances...

One should offer [the consort]. If, out of desire or even delusion, one seeks a woman of low birth, he goes to the Raurava hell by virtue of that union with a woman of low birth. O Goddess! In the Kali age, one should not even mentally recall union with a woman of low birth. She who is engaged in the Kula rites is liberated; of this there is no doubt.

A woman of noble family and a courtesan of noble family should both take refuge in a single hero; having abandoned their animal-like husbands, they should enter the path of the Kula. Having entered the path of the Kula, she should take refuge in a single hero. And if, having set out upon the path of the Kula, she should become husbandless:

Whether she be of noble birth or of high lineage, she is born in a future life devoted to the family dharma and praised for her zeal in the family dharma. O Maheśānī! She is worthy of worship; even one whose husband is lowly should honor her. According to the sequence of worldly custom, she is worthy of worship if she is modest; having abandoned her [otherwise], [one should not do so].

O Mistress of the Kula! One should worship those born of the Kula; by the mere sight of one of noble lineage, the destruction of all sins occurs, just as the destruction of sins occurs by the mere remembrance of the Gaṅgā. She who is born of the Kula and is of noble lineage bestows the fruits of mantra and tantra; she is the Great Courtesan (Mahāveśyā).

She alone shall bestow the fruit of all courtesans—she who is among the perfected sciences (siddhavidyā) praised for worship within the Kula; she alone is specifically proclaimed as the Śakti of all courtesans.
The specific power associated with a specific vidyā has been described in the thirteenth chapter as follows:

The Śyāmā-vidyā will not be accomplished without approaching a Brāhmaṇa woman; Chinnamastā will not be accomplished without approaching a Kāpālinī; the Siddha-vidyā will not be accomplished without the daughter of a king; and Bhairavī, O Goddess, [is found] in the house of a washerwoman.
It is well-accomplished. She is declared to be the one to be attained; when practiced as prescribed, she grants swift success.
One should practice throughout the entire night, with the exception of the Brāhmaṇī and Yāvanī [mudrās].
Abandoning all other undertakings, a twice-born man should practice the Rājarājeśvarī [mudrā] belonging to the twice-born caste.

She is the manifest bearer of the form of a twice-born man’s wife; by merely pleasing such a woman, the beautiful one is swiftly accomplished. One should never employ for practice a lovely woman born of a superior caste;
if she is used in practice, there will be a loss of accomplishment, and one shall go to the Raurava hell.
Now, the ritual application (*prayoga*): When the night has passed its watches, having placed one's own power (*svaśakti*) or another's power (*paraśakti*) upon a couch to one's left,

and having performed the ritual depositions (*nyāsa*) on her limbs as prescribed in one's own ritual manual, [one should perform] purification (*śuddhi*) in the case of one who is uninitiated (*adīkṣitā*).

One should perform [the rite] as follows: *Aiṃ Klīṃ Sauḥ Tripurāyai imāṃ svaśaktiṃ pavitrīkuru mama śaktiṃ kuru svāhā*. Having sprinkled her with drops of water by means of this mantra, one should utter the *māyābīja* into her left ear with the realization of non-duality (*abheda-buddhi*). Then, the *yoni*...
One should meditate thus: [the goddess] with exceedingly graceful limbs, a smiling face, and three eyes;
possessing a beauty that surpasses the clouds, radiant as silken garments; enriched by hands granting the gestures of fearlessness and boon-giving;
most magnificent with jewel ornaments; seated upon a jeweled lion-throne on a pedestal beneath a celestial wish-fulfilling tree.
"I worship Bhavānī in the form of the Yoni—she who is adored by Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Śiva; whose very nature is the purification of the intellect;
who, anointed with the essence of passion, grants the desires of those possessed by longing; whose form is unrestrained in the play of all living beings;
and who destroys the impurities of the Kali age. Having thus meditated upon the Yoni:
Having worshipped and recited the Yoni-mantra "hasauḥ" one hundred and eight times over the yoni, and having offered it, one should recite the hymn,
the armor-verse (kavaca), and so forth, as follows:
The Goddess said:

O Blessed One! Knower of all dharmas! Master who has reached the further shore of the meaning of the Kula scriptures! O Protector, O Supreme Lord, you have indeed told me everything, yet not this one thing—namely, the King of Hymns to Śrīyoni and likewise the supreme armor (kavaca). O Omniscient One, I desire to hear it, if you have compassion for me.
O Mahādeva! This essence, the secret contained within the Vedas, [is held] by me.
O Lord, if it is not told to me, I shall give up my life. O Illustrious One, day and night tears have fallen from me; therefore, O Lord of the gods, let it be told to me.
O Treasure of Compassion!
The illustrious Mahādeva said:
Listen, Pārvatī! I shall tell you how one should perform the renunciation of the body.

Indeed, this was declared of old in the Nigama as something to be kept strictly secret; it was not previously told by me even to Brahmā, Viṣṇu, the planets, and others. O Supreme Goddess, it is unspeakable; what can I do now?

Bound by my affection for you, O beloved! I shall tell it to you, O Mother, O Goddess, O highly fortunate one! But if it is to be revealed to anyone else, O Durgā, take an oath from me that you are remembered as my dear one—even if Brahmā were to appear with four faces or five faces.

Sadāśiva can never describe this King of Hymns; I am not able to speak it fully, so I shall tell it to you in brief. Of this Śrī Yoni-stavarāja, the Kulācārya is the seer (ṛṣi) and Kaulika is the meter (chanda).

The deity whose form is the auspicious *yoni* (womb), consisting of the ten *vidyās*, is to be employed in all spiritual practices (*sādhana*). Oṃ! O you whose form is the *yoni*! O Great Illusion (*Mahāmāyā*)! O bestower of all prosperity! O Auspicious One!
O Goddess who pervades the universe, by your grace grant me all accomplishments (*siddhi*). O you who are the essence of all! *p. 1075)* [End of verse]
O Sovereign of All! O Thou endowed with all powers! "By Your grace," and so forth. || 2 || O Mahāghorā! O Mahākālī!

O Thou who always delightest in the Kula-observance! "By Your grace," and so forth. || 3 || O Thou with terrible fangs! O Ugratārā! O Destroyer of all enemies! "By Your grace," and so forth. || 4 || O Thou whose form is the Yoni!

O Great Knowledge! O Giver of liberation at all times! [Grant me grace... etc. || 5 || O Mother of the World! O Great Knowledge! O Performer of the world’s upliftment! [Grant me grace... etc. || 6 || O Mother of the World! O Great Illusion! O You whose form is the source! O Eternal One! [Grant me grace... etc. || 7 || Victory to You, O Goddess!

O Mother of the World! O You who cause the creation, maintenance, and end [of the universe]! Forgive me, etc. || 8 || O Bestower of Siddhis! O Mahāmāyā! O Bestower of all accomplishments! Forgive me, etc. || 9 || O Mahālakṣmī! O Great Goddess! O Bestower of supreme liberation! Forgive me, etc. || 10 || O Gaurī...

Lakṣmī, Mātaṅgī, Durgā, Navacaṇḍikā, Vagalāmukhī, Bhuvaneśī, Bhairavī, O Dear One! Chinnamastā, Kālī, and the eternal Yonirūpā—out of compassion for me, and so forth... 11. Kālī, Kapālinī, Kullā, Kurukullā, and Virodhinī.
Salutations again and again to those other leaders who are remembered as the leaders such as Vipracittā and others, who dwell taking refuge in the womb;

salutations to You, the bestower of yoga and liberation—salutations to You, salutations to You! (12) The eight supernatural powers, beginning with *aṇimā*, also dwell in her proximity. Salutations to You, salutations to You, O giver of yoga and liberation!

O Goddess, who consists of all power! O destroyer of all impurities! O Yoni! Remove my obstacles and grant me all success. O foundation of all worshippers, O speaker of pleasant words! To the Yoni dwelling in heaven and the netherworld— || 14 ||
And salutations, salutations! || 15 || O Goddess, bestower of Viṣṇu-siddhi! O Goddess, giver of Viṣṇu-siddhi!
O Goddess, bestower of Brahma-siddhi! O giver of siddhi to Rāmacandra! Salutations, salutations to the giver of siddhi to all, beginning with Śakra! || 16 || Thus has it been told to you, O Goddess!

(1076) O Great Goddess! This hymn of the Yoni, which bestows all accomplishments (*sarvasiddhi*), has been revealed to you. O Beloved! O Goddess! O Beautiful One! Whatever Kaulika practitioner recites this hymn that grants all accomplishments, having written it in a book with red substances, for him there is nothing unattainable.

O Mistress of the Family! Ritual acts are perfectly accomplished. There is none, there is none, again there is none, indeed there is none at all within the three worlds [who can surpass him]. That man who, having risen in the morning, recites this, shall attain the status of a leader of the Gaṇas (Gāṇapatya).
That best of practitioners who recites this hymn at night during union with his beloved— [By means of this hymn.]
Having praised her, what could the practitioner not accomplish? Having adorned his own beloved wife—

who is decorated with playful gestures and expressions— and having clothed her in red garments, the practitioner, after worshipping her and feeding her, O Goddess, should then eat himself, being intent upon that goal.

Having eaten fish, meat, and other such foods, and having taken his own wife onto his lap, if one recites the mantra at night, she indeed becomes Durgā and he becomes Sadāśiva; of this there is no doubt, for it has issued from my own mouth. He who gave this hymn to me is remembered as my very guru.

If one should have devotion to this very [text], he would become the Lord of the Universe. Homage be to the King of Hymns; homage to the Illuminator of Hymns. Wherever this King of Hymns resides, there resides Śrī Sadāśiva. Thus, in the *Śaktikāgamasarvasva*, in the dialogue between Hara and Pārvatī.
The Śrīyoni-stavarāja is completed.
Now, the Yonikavaca.
The Goddess said:
"O Blessed One! I desire to hear the most wonderful armor (kavaca). Now, O Lord of the Gods of gods, [reveal] the armor that bestows all perfections. Mahādeva said:

Listen, O Pārvatī! I shall speak, O beloved, of that which is most supremely secret. It must not be given to just anyone; if given [to such], it would become fruitless. Of this *Śrīyonikavaca*, Guptarṣi is the seer (*ṛṣi*), Kulaṭā is the meter (*chandaḥ*), and its application (*viniyoga*) is for the destruction of kings, obstacles, and portents. Hrīṃ.

May the Yoni, the destroyer of obstacles, who is *svāhā*, always protect me. May that Yoni, whose nature is the destruction of enemies, always protect me in the ocean. May the Great Yoni, whose essence is Brahman, protect all my desires. At the most terrible royal gate, may the *klīṃ* Yoni protect me at all times.

The Goddess, whose essence is *Hūṃ*, who is the form of the womb and consists of the universe, may she protect my every limb eternally in the assembly hall and in the royal palace. Sarasvatī, whose essence is the Vedas, who is the womb and the form of the Vedas, [grant] fame, fortune, splendor, and health.

Likewise, [protect] my sons, grandsons, and so forth! Protect, protect me, O Great Source (Mahāyoni)! O Bestower of all Siddhis! May the Yoni, whose essence is the union with the *rajas*, always protect me everywhere. Thus, O Goddess, has this armor (*kavaca*) that grants all Siddhis been told to you; he who recites it daily at the three junctions of the day...
It destroys calamities caused by kings; one becomes a master of speech in the assembly and like a king in the royal palace.

Indeed, by the recitation of this armor (*kavaca*), one attains victory everywhere. O Goddess! if one recites this with undivided mind at the confluence of the Śrī-yoni, he alone shall become the lord of all supernatural powers (*siddhis*); no doubt should be entertained in this matter.

If a person recites [this mantra] after encasing it within the syllables of the Mātṛkā, he shall enjoy vast pleasures and rejoice together with Durgā. Thus, O Goddess, this is the most secret [teaching], the highest of all supreme dharmas; having written it on birch bark or a palm leaf, one should wear it.

If, with yellow pigment (rocanā) mixed with saffron and yellow sandalwood, one [applies it] to the crest-lock or on the neck, he too is Śiva; of this there is no doubt. O Kulasundarī! During the autumn season, on the eighth or ninth day, at the time of worship, one who recites this shall be eternally victorious.
Thus ends the doubt. In the *Śaktikāgamasarvasva*, within the dialogue between Hara and Gaurī, the *Śrīyonikavaca* is completed.
Having thus recited the armor (*kavaca*), performed the six-limbed placement (*ṣaḍaṅganyāsa*) upon her limbs,

performed the placement of the *mātṛkā* and the placement of the *yoni-bīja* in the vulva, and having obtained her permission and offered betel and other offerings, one should recite the *liṅga-mantra*, "Aiṃ," one hundred and eight times over the *liṅga*.

Having recited this and contemplated, "I am Gaurī, and this is Śiva," one should place the father’s face into the mother’s mouth, utter the root mantra, and say: "Oṃ! With the mind as the sacrificial ladle, I perpetually offer the functions of the senses into the fire of the self, which is kindled by the oblation of dharma and adharma, via the path of the *suṣumṇā*. Thus.
Having recited the mantra and inserted the *liṅga* into the *yoni*,

one should contemplate the non-duality of Śiva and Śakti who are absorbed in sexual union; then, remaining unagitated and with a steady mind, one should perform [the recitation] one thousand and eight or one hundred times using a rosary of beads.
Having recited [the mantra] at the end of the root [mantra]:
"Oṃ, with the hands of light and space, taking hold of the ladle of *unmanī*, I offer into the fire that which is filled with the oil of the portions of merit and demerit; svāhā! Thus.

One should discharge the semen with the mantra. O Goddess! If one should utter [the mantra] once during the striking [of the breath], that moment, O lady of tremulous glances, is equal to ten million solar eclipses.
Having taken the "falling moon" (galaccandra), one should prepare the *kuṇḍa* and *goḷa*, etc., even in the case of a woman who has a husband.

The *kuṇḍa* is for a widow, and the *gola* is likewise; having purified it according to the previously mentioned sequence, one should worship and offer libations with that [water]. Then, having washed the *yonipīṭha*, one should recite the root mantra (*mūla*) with that water [to the deity] who is equipped with weapons, accompanied by attendants, and together with the vehicle.
"I satisfy [the goddess] so-and-so, together with Mahākāla, svāhā!"— with this mantra, one should perform the libation three times into the *yoni* and worship her as well.

The Sequence of Commencement: Embracing, kissing, and then the massaging of the breasts; gazing, touching, the expansion of the vulva, the rubbing of the linga, entry, and the induction of the power—these nine are the flowers for worship. The union of Śiva and Śakti is indeed Yoga itself.

There is no doubt. The sound "śīt" is the recitation of mantra; speech shall be praise. Embracing is musk and camphor; kissing is [the application of] these. Scratches from nails and teeth and so forth are various flowers. Sexual union is the libation (tarpaṇa).

Know that the emission of semen is the relinquishment [of the practice]. Having protected the womb with one hundred and eight repetitions, the knower of Dharma who indeed abstains from sexual intercourse shall obtain the entire fruit.
For those engaged in the "creeper" (latā) rite, the mantra should be recited for liberation from great sins, having taken up the state of the menstrual flow (*rajas*).
Having worshipped one's chosen deity at their roots during the dead of night, one should perform the recitation (*japa*) for three days;

one obtains thousands of *lakṣa*-pedestals, of this there is no doubt. If, upon seeing the earth in her fertile state (during menstruation), one performs it daily a thousand times, then one becomes a debater who has mastered the excellent Siddhāntas.

He should enter the surface of the earth. "Constantly" means for sixteen days. That man who, having seen the house of the Kula when it is in bloom, recites [the mantra] to the measure of ten thousand repetitions, shall become a wish-fulfilling tree (kalpapādapa).
Now, the praise of Śakti and so forth, in the fifth chapter:
"O Maheśānī! Without Śakti, I am always of the nature of a corpse. O Devī!
When united with Śakti, I am Śiva, the granter of all desires. One should recite the mantra when it is joined with Śakti; [one should not recite] the mantra [alone]."
One should merely recite [the mantra]. O daughter of the mountain, Brahmā together with Sāvitrī attained perfection!
In Dvārāvatī, Lord Kṛṣṇa attained perfection along with Satyabhāmā. Likewise, O fair-faced one, my perfection arose from union with Kaucabadhū; I am the Lord, O Great Goddess!

It is solely through the application of power. O Goddess of gods! if, by the application of power, perfection (siddhi) does not arise, then, O Supreme Sovereign, my word would be in vain. [Such are] Gaṅgā, Kāśī, Prayāga, Puṣkara, Naimiṣa, as well as Badarī and Revā.

Utkala, Gaṇḍakī, as well as Sindhu and Sarasvatī, and various sacred seats (pīṭhas)—having abandoned all these, O Maheśānī, one should diligently avoid association with women. Through association with women, one attains perfection; my word is not otherwise. That which has been given...
O Goddess of the gods! A mouthful of water [offered] into the mouth of the Śakti becomes the form of the ocean, O Maheśānī;

there is no doubt about this. One should diligently feed her with the realization that she is one's own chosen deity (iṣṭadevī). O Goddess, beautiful as a celestial nymph! Listen, for the nature of the Śakti is now being described.

O beloved Maheśvarī! A woman who is between the ages of thirteen and twenty-five, especially one who has not yet given birth, should certainly perform the fifth [rite] even if she is beautiful, whether she has borne children or not;
it must be performed for every Śakti.

O Goddess! Whoever performs worship and other rites directed toward the five-fold quintuplicated [deity], shall obtain inexhaustible merit; there is no need for deliberation on this point. O beautiful one, one should satisfy the Guru with devotion, as well as his wife and his daughter Lata, with various foods, garments, and other materials, as well as wealth.

And regarding the power that exists for the sake of the fifth [element], one should perform the fifth [rite] within it; listen, O beloved, as I describe how one should specifically perform a hymn of praise therein, with substances and ornaments,
and especially with various kinds of food and drink, as well as with diverse garments and other offerings.

Through kissing and other such acts; now listen to the supreme secret of the deities regarding bathing, by which, O Goddess, when the bath is performed, the deity becomes well-pleased. Having engaged in the fivefold [mudrās] during the night among the five makāras, and within the center of the bhaga...

O Goddess of beautiful countenance! Whatever substance one should diligently take up, that should be known as the water born from the *kuṇḍa*. It is obtained through the power of fortune, being difficult even for the gods to attain. Having poured a little of that water into it, one should place it in a copper vessel.
By the mere act of bathing with that substance, the deity becomes well-pleased.

In the second chapter of the *Uttaratantra*: "The Śakti consists of all sacred seats (*pīṭha*), has the nature of all deities, consists of all mantras, and bestows the four aims of human life. O fair-faced one, for him who regards the Śakti as a mere human being, [there is no success]."
(1080) There would be the attainment of mantra-siddhi, yet one may obtain a contrary result [if the procedure is otherwise].

O Goddess! By the complete worship of Śakti, O Beloved! all the gods are worshipped. O Goddess! whatever clothing, ornaments, and so forth are given to Śakti, O Beloved! that is indeed given upon the body of the Goddess.
O lady of excellent hips!

Whatever garments and ornaments were given to the Goddess, those very same things are now being given here once again, a hundredfold. O lady of excellent hips! Beholding him by whom confusion regarding drinking might arise, and who would feel disgust for blood and semen—[one should observe him].
One of noble birth may fall into the state of a beast.

In the fourteenth chapter of the *Puraścaraṇarasollāsa-tantra*: "In the Kali age, O lady of tremulous glances! in the land of Bhārata, union with women is the supreme state. There is no incense, O fair-complexioned one! no lamp, O lady of tremulous glances! and no food offering as prescribed in the Tantras."

O Beloved! O Maheśānī! The sixteenth substance does not exist; how then will there be accomplishment? Therefore, O Maheśānī! since it consists of eternal bliss, O lady of tremulous glances, worship is established within the limbs of the beloved; for a woman is eternally composed of bliss.
She belongs to oneself, yet her domain is the supreme; O Maheśānī! All sacred fords (tīrthas) truly reside within her limbs.
O Maheśānī! If one abandons her and recites [mantras] at another place, O Goddess! all of that is in vain, and he certainly becomes insane.

In the third chapter of the *Nigamakalpadruma*: "O observer of noble vows! The seven hundred thousand great vidyās have been described to you. These, in the form of mantras, dwell individually within the pores of the skin.
O beloved of the vital breath! As many as are the hairs upon the body, so many are the deities."

And there are goddesses within that body; three crores of holy places (tīrthas) are in the waters of the Jāhnavī for that duration of a year. The Jāhnavī is eternally established at the root of the womb (yonimūla), and in the place of urine, you—Mukti—are always stationed; of this there is no doubt. And Prakṛti...
And the Supreme Brahman is proclaimed as the Puruṣa. Also in the *Yonitantra*: "Kālī, Tārā, Chinnamastikā in the hair-tuft, and Bagalāmukhī and Mātaṅgī dwell near the vulva;
in the triangle is the goddess Tripurā, and by her side is Bhairavī herself."

In the *Puraścaraṇarasollāsa*, [it is said]: "O lady of tremulous glances! In the Kali age, the sacred seats (*pīṭhas*) will become secret. The body of women, endowed with fifty seats, bestows auspiciousness;
how then can the deluded world abandon that great station of womanhood? (p. 1081).

O Dear One! O Pārvatī! In this form, the satisfaction of the gods occurs even at other seats (pīṭhas) and sacred fords (tīrthas). O Dear One! Having then abandoned women, one should go to another seat;
for that woman, O Supreme Goddess, is the manifest embodiment [of the deity] and not otherwise.
"O lady of beautiful limbs! Indeed, the eight supernatural powers (siddhis) arise through union with a woman. Thus ends the praise of Śakti.
Now, the practice of the creeper by another method, as taught in the first chapter of the *Uttaratantra*.

O lady of excellent limbs! For him who writes the letters of the mantra at the base of a creeper with [ink] produced from his own body—that is, from his penis—the mantra becomes perfected. By the mere sight of him, even sinners are liberated. "At the base of a creeper" means at the vulva; "produced from the body" means from the penis.

O Daughter of the Mountain! O Goddess worshipped by the gods! Whatever substance is produced when the Lord of Kalās (the Moon) is joined with the Lord of Kalās (Mercury), that substance is difficult for me to obtain. Indeed, even with thousands of crores of tongues and hundreds of crores of mouths, one would not be able to describe its greatness.
O Supreme Goddess! Rites such as *puraścaraṇa* and others are difficult to accomplish;
this very secret (*śaṅketa*) must be well-guarded here in the presence of the uninitiated (*paśu*). As for the other [method], it is stated in the second chapter:
"He who, having placed the digit (*kalā*) afflicted by the arrows of Kāma upon Śaṅkara, meditates..."
Through devotion alone, he is that very wish-fulfilling tree for Śaṅkara during their inverted dalliance.
Like a bird lured by a beautiful red snare made of vine-roots held in his hand,
he [was drawn] toward sweet food accompanied by condiments and grape juice,
as well as fresh butter and various delicacies.
O Dear One! The supreme face of Rambhā and Rambheśa arises from the Lord of Plantains (Kadalīnātha);
having combined them both into one, with disheveled hair and naked as the directions, one should offer the oblation (bali) either in a crossroads or in a cremation ground, O fair-faced one;
for that Goddess exists in the form of a woman.

The Supreme Goddess grasps [it]. He who is capable of acting in this way is the Blessed Lord himself. O Sovereign of the Gods! In the darkness of night, in the sun, in the face, on the mountain of gold (Meru), in Āvarta, in Kāmarūpa, in Khañjana, in liberation, in duality, and in the bow.
O fair-faced one! O Supreme Goddess! O Beloved! What could be impossible for him who recites [this mantra] upon an image, a sesame flower, a lotus stalk, the earth, or a plantain tree;
or when the hair is dark as the night’s gloom, or on the sun, or within a circle of vermilion, or on the mountain of gold?
In the pair of breasts; in the navel, Āvarta; in the vulva, Kāmarūpa; in the two eyes, Khañjana;
in the two teeth, Muktādvandva; in the eyebrows, Cāpa; in the lips, Vimba;
in the nose, Tilapuṣpa; in the two arms, Padmanāla; and in the two thighs, Dharā and Rambhā.
On the hip.
The Goddess said:

"How indeed, O Mahādeva, could one perform an act through another's power? How could the fault of violating another's wife not arise? How could union with another's wife be performed by means of another? One's status as a virtuous woman is quickly destroyed; therefore, one should not practice this."

Also, in the fourth chapter of the *Vṛhannīlatantra*: "O Goddess! Regarding the practice with another's wife, a censurable discourse prevails; by union with them, O Maheśānī, one would go to the Tāmisra hell. Having understood this to be the meaning of the Vedas, how could a practitioner perform it?"
He establishes the final conclusion on that very point: "One should not approach the wives of others; yet, if one should approach them, one should recite the mantra.
Because of the contradiction between two scriptural statements, one may approach the wives of others. This is also stated in the *Uttaratantra*.

Except at the time of worship, one should not mentally touch any other man. And at the time of worship, O Goddess of Gods! one should satisfy even a prostitute; her status as a virtuous wife is not destroyed by kissing and embracing, O Beloved! [All] the holy places, such as Kāśī and others...
O lady of excellent vows! All merits dwell indeed within her body, as do all mantras, O beautiful one!
No doubt should be entertained by you in this matter, O daughter of the king of mountains!

Now, the worship of the *yoni*. In the first chapter of the *Niruttara-tantra*: "Mahākālī has the form of the *yoni*; the corpse is proclaimed as the bed. O Goddess, O Maheśvarī, the cremation ground (*śmaśāna*) is of two kinds:
the funeral pyre and the *yoni*. Likewise: "O Goddess, whatever [practice] there may be without the worship of the *kalās*..."
An action is performed; that action leads to the accomplishment of the rite (*abhicāra*), truly, truly, there is no doubt.

Therefore, with every effort, one should perform the worship of Kalā. O Goddess! Kalā is of the form of the Yoni, she is indeed the South, there is no doubt. O lady of beautiful hips! The divine hero [should perform] the worship of Kalā.
One should practice thus: a practitioner who relies on the state of a *paśu* (bound soul) must not worship the *kalā* at all.
O Kuleśvarī! The worship of the *kalā* is of two kinds: secret and manifest.
That which is secret should be performed by practitioners in a secluded place during the dead of night; the manifest worship should be performed during the day.
However, it must be done according to the sequence of worldly conduct. O Goddess, without worldly conduct, concealment does not occur at all.

Concealment is the root of accomplishment; this is the truth, the truth—there is no doubt. O beautiful lady of noble family, whether one be a Brāhmaṇa, Kṣatriya, Vaiśya, or Śūdra, through the yoga of the essence of the Kalās...

One should perform the worship of Kalā. In the absence of the prescribed materials, a twice-born man should offer a substitute in each age; the substitute for Kalā is the contemplation of Kalā itself. O Goddess! Without the worship of Kalā, a sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā) does not yield fruit.
The wife is the symbol of one's own chosen deity (*iṣṭadevatā*).

Thus it is said in the second chapter of the *Samayācāra-tantra*: "Now, I shall explain briefly the worship of the *bhaga* (vulva). That mantra which one constantly recites by the grace of the Guru..."

The practitioner, the master of mantras, performs the worship of the *bhaga* with that very mantra. At that time, he should indeed contemplate her in the form of the *bhaga* within the center of the *bhaga*. Having become Śiva, he should remember the Goddess and perform that very union.
He should then contemplate the Śakti as being composed of Śakti; that indeed is the sexual union (*maithuna*).

One should practice; through the yoga of attachment to sexual union, one should perform mental recitation (*japa*). O Goddess! he who performs what has been taught attains the supreme state. Whatever mantras have been declared, O fair-faced one, they are certainly to be recited, O Queen of the Gods, in all the Tantras. And likewise:

O Goddess! The merit that arises from the remembrance of Bhaga, as well as from the sight of Bhaga, and the merit produced by the touch of Bhaga—that happiness is not attained through recitations, fire-offerings, meditations, or asceticism. O Goddess! [This is the fruit] when five times five have been performed.
Merit is produced on earth; yet, O fortunate one, that merit is not attained even by seeing Koṭitīrtha.

Recitation, fire-offerings, likewise charity, initiation, and the practice of yoga and other disciplines do not equal even a sixteenth part of the merit of one who has observed the fifth meal (the fast).

In the sixth chapter of the *Nigamakalpadruma*: "Having performed the worship of the *yoni* (source) without [the preliminary rites of] invocation and so forth, one should worship one's chosen deity within that *yoni* with the root mantra (*mūlamantra*).
One should worship it thoroughly with that *yoni*-mantra, which is the *māyābīja*, according to one's own capacity. (p. 1084)

One should worship with the yoga of devotion to the limit of one's resources. Then, the best of practitioners should mutter the mantra one hundred times within the womb. Then, while contemplating the desired form, one should place the *liṅga* in the *bhaga*.
Kulabhairava should press her firmly according to his own capacity. Upon the impact—

The moon (Sudhākara) destroys even a hundred murders of Brahmins. Through engagement with the Kāmaśāstra, as satisfaction may arise, the excellent practitioner should repeatedly apply [the substance] to the mouth for that purpose. At the time of the emission of semen and so forth, the noble-minded one should recite the mantra. Thereafter, however—
Taking the substance, one should offer it to Mahādevī. Having done this, O Mahādevī, one shall not be born again in a womb. This is the truth, the absolute truth, O Mahādevī; this is my supreme yoga.
What is the use of speaking much here? Listen, O beloved of my life!

In the sixth chapter of the *Vṛhannīlatantra*: "Alternatively, if the vision of one who can assume any form at will (*kāmarūpa*) should arise, then the worship of the goddesses, beginning with Bhaga, is prescribed there. If, by the power of fortune alone, the vision of the *kula* should arise, then that very [vision] is mental worship."
Therein, one should assign them as follows: Bhaginī, Bhagajihvā,
Bhagāsyā, Bhagamālinī, Bhagāṅgā, Bhagākṣī,
Bhagavarṇā, Bhagatvacā, Bhagastanī, Bhaganāśā, Bhagasthā, and Bhagasarpiṇī.

There, having worshipped the Guru with mental offerings of perfumes and the like, and having prostrated according to the rule, the wise man himself remains undisturbed. As stated in the *Nigamakalpadruma*:
"The vulva, or the lotus of the breasts, the sun, the black lotus, the fly-whisk, or the hips..."
If a vision [of her] arises, then one should bow down again and again and recite the King of Mantras.

O Great Goddess! for them as well, liberation is held in the palm of their hand. He who, devoted to devotion, drinks the water from the feet of Śakti, or even consumes her remnants (ucchiṣṭa), [attains that same state].

His success shall be unimpeded, O Śivaṅkarī! If faith in my words arises, then the word spoken by me shall be acted upon; otherwise, one should not do so. If, at the time of the pilgrimage, he goes after smelling the *yonitattva* and holding his hair upon his head, [then his success is assured].
The enemy perishes; he shall be victorious in the assembly hall and likewise in royal affairs.
This is the truth, O illustrious lady! My word is never in vain. By whatever means possible, one who is devoted to the worship of the Yoni goes to the supreme abode.

It is extremely difficult even for the gods to obtain. Whether in a state of extreme distress, in the palace of a king, or during a great calamity or portent, if one worships the Yoni, then the Great Goddess Yoni shall deliver one from every danger. There is nothing superior to this that exists for me.
From his words: "This is true, there is no doubt, if I am your beloved;

having abandoned all other dharma, one should become devoted to the worship of the Yoni. Only then is supreme joy attained, and one reaches the state of absolute freedom from shame. Just as among all waters, that of the Gaṅgā..."

"Just as clarified butter is the best among products derived from cows, so too, O Goddess! O Beloved! may sexual union be most dear to me. [From the *Nigamakalpadruma*: "One should place both thighs upon the thighs of the beloved;
having grasped her neck with both hands, one should press the pair of breasts."
In various places, there is kissing in many ways upon the face; this is the "Beautiful with Passion" (Kāmasundara) embrace.

Having placed the penis into the vagina, with both feet resting upon the hands, and seizing the hair with both hands while pressing the pair of breasts moment by moment, one performs kissing upon all the limbs.

One should repeatedly drink from the lower lip; one should take delight with a firm strike—this is the "Expert in Pleasure" (Ratipaṇḍita) posture. One should place the feet upon the shoulders, insert the penis into the womb, and, having seized the head with both hands, proceed with a sequence of biting the teeth while kissing.
Rubbing the eyes, the face, and the breasts repeatedly, the lover should take his pleasure according to his ability;
this is the "Crushing of Desire" (Kāmamardana) posture.
Having placed her upon one's chest, with her thighs over one's thighs, and having pressed her cheeks with both hands while grasping her shoulders—this is another [posture].

Preceded by a kiss, one should take delight with very firm blows; this is the "Kāmakautuka" bond. O Goddess of gods! O Bhairavī! In this manner, there are many bonds, as revealed in their entirety in the Kāmaratna and other Tantras. [This is] the special bond.
In brief, this has been urged against you by way of a consequential argument.

Now, the sixteen postures (*bandha*). In the *Ratirahasya*: "Eighty-four postures have been proclaimed by the Sage; therefore, having extracted from them those sixteen which are the causes of love, they are written here. Having placed his feet upon the two shoulders of the woman, he inserts his organ into her womb."
Brief: A lustful man should desire a woman; for that is indeed the "crow's foot" (kākapada) position.

Holding one foot in the hand and placing the second upon the shoulder, the lover should desire the woman; this is the *veṇuvidāraka* bond. If the man places his hands upon the woman’s pair of thighs at the base of her loins and holds her neck with both hands, it is the *nāgaraka* bond.
If a beautiful woman presses [the man] with her pair of thighs, O lover, it is declared to be the *ratipāśa* (love-noose),
which brings happiness to passionate women. Having firmly embraced the beautiful woman with his arms while positioned between her shanks, the lover should perform the *bandhana* (bond).

The embrace known as "the Peacock": if the lover holds the woman's feet with his own hands at her throat, while placing his hands upon her breasts, this is indeed the graceful embrace. Placing one foot on her heart and resting the second on her shoulder, the lovers should take delight while holding her breasts.

The *bandha* (posture) known as *stanabhara* is described as follows: the lover should hold the two feet of the woman against the circle of her breasts; holding her by the neck, he should enjoy the woman—this is the *bandha* called *ratisundara*. Furthermore, having grasped the woman's two thighs with both hands, he should press them together.

The lustful one should intensely desire this union of pleasure, which is a bond; holding her thigh with the left hand and placing his foot upon her head, the lustful one should enjoy her very firmly—this is proclaimed as the *smaracakra*. [Holding her] between both of his own knees...

One should hold the woman firmly; with no hesitation, the lover [should apply] this "Nāgapāśaka" (Snake-noose) bond on the left side. Having drawn both of the woman's feet toward himself, the lover, with his face turned away, should press against her *yoni*;
this bond is named "Kuliśa" (Thunderbolt). Such are the arrangements of these bonds.

Intense pleasure is produced [thereby]. Therefore, bonds should be applied with effort by those skilled in the art. A bond should be employed with one's whole being whenever the hero experiences pleasure; for through that, desire indeed arises in the man during sexual union. [The woman...]
Having sequentially grasped her from behind with the forearms and the cheeks, one should then take pleasure in her abdomen;
this is the "Ratisundara" (Beautiful in Love) bond. If a woman seated on the bed raises her hips and desires her lover, this is the "Kavargasaṅgama" (Conjunction of the Ka-group) bond.

Thus, two [positions] with faces turned downward should be performed. Having raised one leg and placed the other on the ground, the lover should take his pleasure with her leaning against a wall; this is known as the *dolāyita* (swinging) bond.
Having quickly embraced the beautiful woman, encircling her waist with both feet, and having kissed her...

The mouth of the beloved is considered the "Lord of Serpents" (Nāgeśvara) position. Having embraced the woman comfortably and kissed her face repeatedly, one should draw the beloved’s waist toward oneself and hold her against one's own neck; this is indeed the "Quick Movement of Desire" (Kāmacālana).
A firm man should bestow [this embrace]. Having placed both her feet upon the thighs of her lover, she who gazes at his waist—this is known as the *sapada* (with-foot) bond.
A woman standing for her lover’s sport with both feet placed on the ground, [and] upon the chest...

The "given-hand" (*dattahasta*) is a bond; the "supreme play-fire" (*līlānalottama*) is inverted intercourse (*vīparītarati*). When the beloved licks the vulva of the beautiful woman into whom the phallus has been inserted, it is likewise called the "box" (*saṃpuṭaka*); such is the engagement of the female organ. This is the "pleasurable union" (*sukharata*). Thus, in the *Śrīprāṇatoṣiṇī*.
The seventh section, the Nirguṇajñānakāṇḍa, consisting of five clusters of flowers,
is completed.

Now, the medicinal formula: In the twenty-first chapter of the *Matsyasūkta*: "Having prepared a lamp, one should then drop soot into a copper vessel; having stirred it with cow's ghee, one should then apply it to the eyes.
One will then see whatever form [was seen] in another birth. (1)

O Goddess of the Gods! Whoever wears kākamācī and the root of the dakṣa plant on their crest induces sleep and even removes the pain of a hemiplegia (ardha-śūla). Having prepared the juice of the leaves of black tulasī with honey, sugar-cane juice, and oil, one should [cook it] over a mild fire.
Then one should apply heat; O Goddess! by applying heat to the ear, one removes ear-ache and other such ailments. || 3 ||
Bhṛṅgarāja and sāranāla will then remove even half-earache. By filling the ear with the juice of jambu leaves, the ear-worm will fall out quickly at night;
there is no doubt one should administer this. Having bound the root and leaves of sahadevā to the ear...
It shall remove the pain. One should fill the eyes with the juice of the Hastiśuṇḍā leaf;
it quickly removes eye pain, as does the Bṛhadasoma gem.

O beloved! By grinding the juice of ginger and neem leaves and applying it to the eyelids on the fifth lunar day, eye pain is destroyed. Furthermore, one should grind the root of *apāmārga*, yellow pigment (*rocanā*), pine resin (*sarala*), along with *mustaka* from a cow, in a copper vessel.

O Goddess! By applying collyrium to the eyes, all pain is destroyed. O Maheśānī! By offering mustard oil, salt, and *vāranāla* with the juice of black *tulasī* leaves on a Tuesday, [the disease] in the eyelid—namely, *paṭala*—is cured.

It goes to destruction. O Goddess! On a Saturday at night, one should cook the flesh of a goat, the meat of a tree-dweller (wild animal), and likewise that of a buffalo, as well as the meat of a monitor lizard and its tongue, in a fire of *khadira* wood; in an instant, it destroys the blindness of night. || 10-11 ||

One should collect three fruits as soft as cotton during the Svāti constellation; O Goddess, by chewing them and filling the eyes with the juice, [eye disease] is destroyed. There is no doubt regarding eye diseases, and likewise listen to [the remedy for] timira (blindness) through the application of red sandalwood mixed with honey.
O beautiful one! How much more does collyrium from Raudraka destroy cataracts, even when it is slightly warm? || 13 ||
By applying a *vaṭa* fruit mixed with honey to the back of the eye, one quickly removes disease;
likewise, one should apply fresh [juice]. One should eat [the fruit] fried in ghee, which greatly increases the luster of the eyes. Or, [one may use] the leaf of *nimba* resin together with oil.
O Goddess! By consuming it, the eye becomes endowed with luster; it is like the staff of the spear of Pāmarī.

Likewise, it removes disease as effectively as coconut water. O Mistress of the Gods! Triphalā mixed with jaggery, or jaggery combined with fresh ginger—by taking these two in the morning, [one is freed] in an instant.
It destroys jaundice. || 17 || One should eat the *dhātrī* fruit with hot water;

thus the disease is destroyed. The marrow of old *kaṇṭakī* and that of *vāsantikā* should be infused three times with mustard oil that is slightly warm; by mere application [as an ointment], [the disease is cured].
It destroys all forms of *vicarcikā* (eczema). O Goddess of the Gods! Having dried and burnt the bark of the *caladala* tree, one should apply it as a warm ointment with mustard oil or castor oil;
this destroys *vicarcikā*, as does *tālamūla* and the seed of the wild pepper (*vanamarīca*). || 18–19 ||

Especially during the dark fortnight, O Goddess! by applying a plaster made with goat’s milk, one destroys all types of eczema (*vicarcikā*), as well as *ajīpalamūlakā*—of this there is no doubt. Then, having burnt dry *māna* [grain] and mixed it with conch-shell powder (*śaṅkhacūrṇa*), one should apply it to the eczema on the limbs.
