One should kill [the disease] by applying it as a paste for three nights. By eating dried and aged *deśimāna* together with ghee, one quickly removes *aṅgavāta*, *paṭustha*, *kṣaṇa*, and *markaṭa*. Having procured that which is three years old and of the *deśimāna* measure...
O Pārvatī! Having made an incision and then applying this ointment, it is the supreme remedy for knots and wind-disorders.

O fair-faced goddess! Having cooked *cakaśā*, radish, and *kola* together with honey and rock salt (*saindhava*), along with fish, using *śāsulla* [fuel], it is the supreme destroyer of wind (*vāta*), O Goddess;
it removes heat, of this there is no doubt. In all cases of wind-disorder, massage with sesame oil is also recommended.
O Pārvatī! Likewise, O beloved, with the oil of the krauñca bird or with snake-oil (nāgataila), || 25 ||

One should saturate [the medicine] with sesame oil, milk, and goat’s milk; this destroys *śrīpada* of the vāta type as well as waist-wind (*kaṭivāta*). [The ingredients are: *unmatta*, *kumbharūpa*, the leaf of *viśāḍhakī*, along with its root, *aṭasāra*, and *vāsaka*.

The dwelling of Rāma: one should place the yoga-leaf along with the *bheruṇḍa* in a clay pot and heat it over the fire of the sun, O Goddess! Then one should again form a pill. The substance consisting of the root of the *arka* plant combined with the root of *snuhī* should be consumed for three days in all types of wind disorders.

It perishes. || 27 || The seeds from the root of *tulasī* and the seeds of *kumārī*, when used as a paste, destroy all types of leprosy (*kuṣṭha*), and even *jalasāra* is eliminated. Having extracted *hastikarṇa* from a *tulā* measure, O fair-faced one, along with the root of *snuhī*, the root of *vilva*, and black pepper—
Taken with sugar, one *tola* at a time for seven days destroys even severe wind-disorders (*mahāvāta*).

O Goddess! By specifically binding the bark of the *kalivṛkṣa* tree around the neck, the destruction of the *okas* is proclaimed, as well as that of the *pāmarīśūlaka*. By grinding the seeds of the *tintiḍī* tree and using them in combination with buttermilk (*takra*), drinking it quickly removes the *āmavīja* from the bladder.

One should quickly remove the growth of gums with the seeds of *vārtākī*; likewise, one may remove it by means of fomentation (*sveda*) using a ripe *vārtāku* fruit over a fire of cow-dung (*karoṣa*). Furthermore, by applying a paste of the root of white *aparājitā* mixed with urine inside the mouth, one certainly destroys numbness.

O Goddess! By uprooting white guñjā under the Puṣya asterism and applying it as an ointment, the disease of poison is destroyed at that very moment. Likewise, blue-throated [viṣṇukrāntā] mixed with honey destroys disease. So too does the root of white aparājitā.

One should then have a white *jayantī* plant and a white *citraka* made into a pill. O Goddess, having uprooted it according to the prescribed rite under the constellation Svāti at moonrise, and having applied a tilaka-mark on the forehead with this, it becomes an excellent means of subjugation. [Likewise,] the seed of the *palāśa* tree, together with honey and ghee...
One should grind [these ingredients]. By consuming [this] for just one month, wrinkles and gray hair are destroyed. || 27 ||

O Goddess, by applying a paste of *vṛhatī*, *nīlakaṇṭha*, and the three myrobalans (*triphalā*) along with salts to the teeth, even toothache is removed. By eating goat meat with goat’s milk and rice-water, as well as *tālamūlī*, one destroys consumption (*yakṣma*), leprosy (*kuṣṭha*), and other such ailments. (38-39)
One should likewise take the root of *nāgakeśara* with honey;

or by placing *yaṣṭīmadhu* and honey in the mouth, one will undoubtedly destroy [the affliction]. By drinking a decoction of its leaves, all fevers are warded off; and by drinking it together with honey as well.

It removes fever during the rainy season. O beloved! By uprooting the root of white Aparājitā when the sun has not yet risen on a Sunday coinciding with the Puṣya asterism, and likewise by wearing it, or similarly by binding a thread from an unmarried girl to an Apāmārga plant, one shall destroy fever, O Maheśānī!

O beloved! On the day of Svātī or Viṣṇu (Śravaṇā), especially on a Sunday, one should take the root of *raktavāṭyāla* and, having bound it with plantain fibers (*kadalīsūtra*), cause it to be placed upon a bed;
this will then destroy all fevers and likewise remove fevers born of heat. One should also [use] the bark of the *kuddāla*.
Likewise, the bark of the Arjuna tree, when drunk together with clarified butter, removes all types of cough.

O Śaṅkarī! The root of Nāgeśvara taken with honey destroys abdominal enlargement; likewise, Viṣṇukrāntā does the same. One should cause [the patient] to drink Pippalī combined with Saindhava salt and honey; thereby, it will destroy the discharge of urine within seven days—of this there is no doubt.
Doubt [remains]. || 47 || Then one should cause [the patient] to drink the root of the *vilva* together with *guḍūcī* mixed with honey;

it destroys vomiting, there is no doubt. The seed of the *mātuluṅga*, || 48 || and the seed of the *palāśa* along with *siddhārtha*, combined with honey and oil—by eating these in equal proportions, one [overcomes] fevers.

It destroys [the disease], there is no doubt. O beloved! Likewise, when bhallātaka is combined with an equal amount of sesame paste, O Goddess, an extremely powerful digestive fire is produced within three nights; of this there is no doubt. (49–50)

Then, one should prepare pills from *candramūlī*, long pepper (*pippalī*), ginger (*śuṇṭhī*), and black pepper (*marica*), using old jaggery. Through this practice of Śiva-yoga, a very strong digestive fire arises quickly upon consumption. [This is done] with the wing of a crow-owl (*kākolūka*).

The wise one should offer incense; it destroys that fear, as well as [the fear] of a moving elephant. (p. 1091) Incense made from equal parts of the wing of a peacock (*nīlakaṇṭha*) and the slough of a serpent (*bhujaga*), when prepared as before, certainly brings about the same result. (53)
Having taken the red flower of the Hayamāra plant, along with sour juice and vetasa, the wise man should thoroughly wipe a mirror with it; then, with undistracted mind,
he shall see the forms of horses, camels, and donkeys.
One should take the nail of a pig, a horse, a donkey, and likewise of a monkey;
then one should burn them in a fire of leaf-cups (*puṭāgni*). Afterwards, one should polish a mirror with the urine of a frog; one will see their forms therein—of this there is no need for doubt.

During the seven days following the period of menstruation of an unfortunate woman, a wise man should place white mustard seeds into her womb. Whosoever touches her while she is eating those mustard seeds shall surely go [to her]. One should likewise take the oil from the seed of the *aṅkoṭha* tree.

Then, one should cut the *mocike* [plant]; its very desire-granting quality brings about strength, nourishment, and supreme increase of longevity. The fruit and leaf of the *jambīra*, combined with *saindhava* salt, serve as a potent application for the teeth.
Likewise, the flower of the *māṣa* [bean] with ghee and boiled rice [is used for similar purposes].

It increases longevity, and strength shall endure for a long time. In the meat of the tortoise, strength is diminished, as is the meat of the *koraka* bird; one indeed goes quickly to a short life by means of the meat of the swan, O Pārvatī! [The same applies to] the *śīkara* of the betel nut.
Combined with the mud of *snuhī*, or with meat, or with the milky sap of *arka* and the fruit of *mandāra*; combined with *rajanī* for wind disorders (*vāta*), or with *tālamūlī* and rice;
and when there is powerlessness and loss of appetite, one should administer it for diseases of the tongue, O Kuleśvarī! [Also] *parpaṭa*.

One should offer curd-rice mixed with jaggery; having made it warm, one should have the patient drink it and then apply it as an ointment to the navel. For diseases of phlegm (kapha) and throat-obstruction (galagraha), one should use the root of the *aśoka* tree and oil-cake (*piṇyāka*).
Likewise, for diseases of the testicles, one should use *parṇaśirā*, *māṇamūla*, and *tālamūla*.
The *kuṣmāṇḍa* in cases of wind-dominance (*vātasāra*), and the *śirīṣaka*; [this is from] the twenty-third chapter.

For toothache and for disorders of wind (*māruta*), one should use rock salt (*saindhava*), long pepper (*pippalī*), and the root of *dantisāra* to pacify dental diseases. For wounds, insect bites, and eruptions,
the tip of the *mandāra* flower mixed with powder and the milky sap of *snuhī* causes the insect to fall away.
"At that very moment. Thus, in the case of cows and the like being wounded, direct perception (pratyakṣa) is to be observed.

p. 1092) Now, O Maheśānī, I shall describe the medical treatment for horses. To one that has vomited, one should give a paste (*piṇḍa*) consisting of *palala* (sesame paste), ginger, long pepper (*pippalī*), *yamānī*, coconut, the root of *muṇḍavāsaka*, *kośala*, and jaggery; this removes the fever.
Supreme!
Cumin, resin of the *sarja* tree, *kola*, durva grass, and *dhanyāka*, combined with *yogapatra*, *gimāśāka*, black pepper, and salt, along with the root of the spring creeper (*vāsantī*)—
this triple-mark (*tripuṇḍra*) removes fatigue. Having gathered the roots and leaves of the great water-plant (*vṛhatpānīya*).
The seed-leaf (*bījapatraka*), ginger (*śṛṅgavera*), barley (*yava*), and the two types of turmeric (*haridrā*)—

this bolus (*piṇḍa*) removes wind disorders and is supreme for bestowing strength and nourishment. Wild jujube (*araṇyabadarī*), *sūkti*, and the dwelling-place of Rāma in the forest (*kānane rāmavāsaka*), along with the seed of the date palm (*kharjūra*) and jaggery, shall remove fever.
One should administer *dhānyamūla*, *ravimūla*, and *kālañjara* together with *somadhānya*;
this destroys the disease of vomiting (*chardikā*). Likewise, *apāmārga*, *viḍaṅga*, *saindhava*, and *nāgakeśara*, combined with *saindhava*, [cures] bird-disease (*pakṣiroga*).

It perishes. In the case of *carcikā* (leprosy), the oil of a frog and that of a *bheruṇḍaka* (a type of lizard) should be applied with a preparation of *niśā* (turmeric); it destroys all types of leprosy. Having burnt the powder of the *madhuvṛkṣa* (mango tree) with the oil of *nāgeśvara*, one should apply the ointment; O Goddess, [the disease] shall perish.
Eczema.
In the twenty-sixth chapter: One should eat the flowers of the *dānava* tree smeared with clarified butter;

this destroys the flow of blood during menstruation, the ritual bath after menses, and *jalandhāra*. Facing the northern direction, one should wrap [the area] with a thread from a virgin, as well as *viṣṇukrāntā* and *apāmārga*.
Cumin and black pepper—one should drink these individually; having drunk them, a pregnant woman will give birth easily.
Likewise, O Goddess of Gods, having smeared the linga and the ground with buffalo butter and *kavikalākṣata*, it shall become [fertile] thereafter. And likewise, the root of the red *bheruṇḍa*...
Having ground together caladalapadmaka, marīca, and priyaṅgu,
one shall increase the size of the penis.

One should drink a single *guvāka* flower together with cow’s milk under the asterism Svāti or on one’s birthday; then, even if she is barren, she shall become pregnant. Furthermore, one should eat the root of *hastiśuṇḍī* and the nose of a sparrow fried in ghee; thus, one’s virility becomes powerful.
It would be so.
In the second chapter of the *Kakṣapuṭa* composed by Nāgārjuna.

O Goddess! One should grind earth from the root of a banyan tree with water; when combined with holy ash (*vibhūti*), this *tilaka* brings the world under one's control. Furthermore, by tying the roots of *punarnavā*, *rudantī*, and likewise *mūlikā* and *yava* around the neck during the *puṣya* asterism—
Consecrated seven times with this mantra, one becomes honored everywhere; the mantra for this purpose is stated here:

*Aiṃ puraṃ kṣobhaya bhagavati gambhīre lkau svāhā*. One should recite this mantra twenty thousand times (*ayutadvaya*); thereafter, success (*siddhi*) is attained. [The ingredients are: *ugrā*, *ātapatra*, and *mañjiṣṭhā*.

Saffron and *tagara* in equal parts, when applied during bathing, drinking, or physical contact, will surely bring about subjugation (*vaśya*). By gathering the root of *siṃhī* under the asterism of Puṣya and binding it around one's waist, one becomes beloved by the world. On the night of the fourteenth day of the dark fortnight, [one should take] great indigo from a cremation ground.
Having extracted it with human oil and an ointment, one gains power over others.

(4) One should bind its root to the hand; one will become beloved by all people. (5) Having extracted the root of the *brahmadaṇḍī* under the Puṣya asterism, [it should be used] in the food of all living beings.

This is the supreme method of subjugation. A wise person, using the heart of an owl mixed with the *rocana* of a virgin, should apply it as an ointment; by this ointment, one shall bring even the three worlds under one's control. Oṃ namo yakṣiṇi amukaṃ vaśamānaya svāhā oṃ. Of this mantra...
Having first recited [the mantra] ten thousand times, then all applications, such as the fierce parasol and so forth, are performed.
The medicinal herb becomes perfected when consecrated one hundred times. For all mantras, the visualization of the mantra is distinct for each; it is to be done in its respective place.
If the specific number is not mentioned, one should recite it ten thousand times. Under the asterism Mṛgaśīrṣa, one should take a deep-red karavīra flower;
a nine-finger-long stake consecrated seven times with mantras, when buried in the ground under someone's name, will certainly bring that person under one's control. Oṃ huḥ huḥ.
Svāhā! Having first recited this one hundred and eight times, a person should then begin [the rite].

In the third chapter: Saffron, sandalwood, and yellow pigment (rocanā) mixed with *śimi*, along with cow’s milk, form a supreme forehead mark (*tilaka*) that brings kings under one's control. *Oṃ hrīṃ saḥ, [name], bring [him] under control, bring [him] under control, svāhā!* One should first perform [this] a thousand times.
Then, having recited this mantra, one should apply the *tilaka* as before: "Oṃ hrīṃ, O Raktacāmuṇḍā, act, act! Bring so-and-so under my control, svāhā!
By means of these Cāmuṇḍā mantras, one becomes accomplished in all things. [Mañjiṣṭhā]

Saffron, *bālā*, *modā*, and *kumārikā*, as well as funeral ashes and one’s own blood, should be processed according to the prescribed rules. Having formed a pill under the asterism Puṣya, one should cause it to be given with food and drink; whether asked or not, the king shall be brought under control.
By the power of the fierce mantra. || 8 ||

Now, victory in debate: Gojihvā or Śikhimūla, when placed in the mouth or on the head, secured under the Puṣya asterism, brings victory in all disputes. One should uproot Śikhimūla on the full moon day of Mārgaśīrṣa; [it should be worn] on the arm or on the head.

If it is worn during a dispute, victory shall be attained; a living being is released from bondage by the *śikhā-mantra*, of this there is no doubt. (2) Furthermore, the root of the *meghanāda* plant encircled within a wheel causes one who commits adultery with another's wife to become mute or else to flee to the ends of the earth.

On the night of the fourteenth day of the dark fortnight, having taken mahānīlī from a cremation ground, one should bind it upon the hand; in dispute, victory shall be attained. A root combined with white guñjā, when held in the mouth, conquers the mouths of the wicked. And for the success of the aforementioned applications, the Caṇḍa-mantra must be employed.

The mantra is: *oṃ sudarśanāya huṃ phaṭ svāhā*. Having first recited it ten thousand times for the sake of accomplishing the Caṇḍa-mantra, the medicinal preparation shall then be consecrated seven times with this mantra. During the bright fortnight under the Puṣya asterism, [one should take] the root of the *guñjā* plant.
One should extract it; when bound upon the head, all of that is supremely effective for removing the affliction of thieves.
In the first chapter of the *Yogasāra*, the words of the Goddess:
I shall describe the destruction of disease: one should drink a *pala* measure of clarified butter while reciting this mantra.
That best of practitioners who drinks it while reciting this mantra will undoubtedly be liberated from all diseases. I shall now declare the mantra for that; listen, O most excellent Bhairava!

*Tāra* (Om), *māyā* (Hrīṃ), *bhṛgu* (Śa), *śambhu* (Ha), then *bhṛgu* (Śa) is proclaimed; joined with *sṛṣṭi* (Kṣa), then *guru* (Sa), and likewise *candra* (Sa) is remembered as *śiva*. This mantra is fully declared and is called "the purification by ghee" (*ghṛtaśuddhi*). || 1 ||

I shall describe the destruction of thirst: taking one *tolaka* of red sandalwood and rubbing it in the left hand, the best of practitioners should mix that *tolaka* with water and recite the mantra one hundred and eight times over it; whoever drinks this [shall have their thirst destroyed].
O Bhairava! For the supreme practitioner, the destruction of craving arises within seven days.
O Kuleśvara! It is taught that for all [substances], consumption should take place over seven days.
Having recited [the mantra], the practitioner should drink everything—one hundred and eight times—using the two seed-syllables of sound.

"O auspicious one! One should utter 'Nāśayadvitayaṃ' (destroy the pair), then pronounce the word 'tṛṣṇā' (thirst), and then 'svāhā'; this is considered the mantra. O Lord! By means of this mantra, the destruction of thirst is produced. || 2 ||

O Lord of the Gods! For the purpose of destroying [the enemy's] food, one should collect black and variegated [substances] in a quantity of half a *tola*, or half of that, or half of that again. Having brought them, the wise one should fashion pills with this mantra; O Lord of the Gods! having mixed them with clarified butter, [he should do so] with this mantra.

One should consume [it]. Having uttered the seed-syllable of desire (KĀM), then the word "O Destroyer of Hunger" (kṣunnāśini), and having spoken the word "ward off" (nivāraya), followed by "svāhā"—this is considered the mantra. || 3 ||
Alternatively, the cessation of hunger is prescribed by another method: first, one should eat sacrificial food (haviṣya);
afterwards, one mutters the Mātṛkā; and thereafter, O Śaṅkara, ghee should be consumed with this mantra: *hasauḥ*, by which the best of practitioners may eat. || 4 ||
Alternatively, O God, having diligently stirred the tongue with clarified butter,
Kulabhairava, one should wipe the tongue as long as it remains covered by the lips, until the tongue is brought to the level of the lips. By this very method, the cessation of hunger will occur.

5 || Or else, another method for the cessation of hunger is prescribed: O Lord of Gods! the knower of mantras daily drinks the smoke of Vijayā through the aperture of Brahma (brahmarandhra), and the destruction of hunger certainly occurs. I shall now declare the Brahma-mantra by which [this is accomplished].

It shall be the destroyer of hunger. O God, Kuleśvara! Having thus recited these three seed-syllables—Sambartaka, Candra, Vahni, and Bhautika—conjoined with the Bindu; and having purified the *vijayā* (marijuana) smoke by means of this mantra, O God, one may drink the smoke, and no fault shall arise.
Hara! || 6 || Now, for the purpose of curing urinary disorders, I shall declare the supreme mantra.

Having procured *aśvagandhā*, one should consecrate it with the *astra-mantra*. O Lord, the wise person, having mixed one *tolaka* of it with clarified butter, should drink it while muttering the *kāmabīja* at the base of the penis.
One should indeed fix it with the mind. Thirty-two *tolakas* of milk and two *tolakas* of black pepper should be mixed together and cooked carefully until it becomes dry;
then, having recited the *vāgbhava* [syllable], the best of practitioners should consume it by this very means.

By this procedure, the destruction of urine occurs. (7) For the purpose of destroying feces, one should take two *tolakas* of *viḍaṅga*, one *tolaka* of *pippalī*, and three *tolakas* of *śuṇṭhī*. Having mixed these with the ash of *tejapatra*, one should recite the mantra.

Having recited it one hundred and eight times, one should mix [the ingredients] with great effort. O Ananabhairava, listen as I declare the mantra for that: Śrī, Māyā, and Vāgbhava—these are the three seed-syllables of Śakti; then Śiva, Vāyu, Jala, Pṛthvī, and finally Vahni-jāyā.
Having recited the mantra, one should drink the substance; it will certainly cause the excrement to disappear.

I shall now describe the immobilization of semen (*śukrastambha*); listen, O best of my Bhairavas! Having ground the root of the castor plant (*eraṇḍa*), one should smear it at the base of the navel. O Śiva, one should smear that same root with the bile of a Rohita fish, having consecrated it with the seed-syllables of sound; thus one shall immobilize it.
Regarding semen and blood: having extracted the seed-syllable of sound (*śabda-bīja*), one should crush it while reciting the weapon-mantra (*astra-mantra*).
Thus it is said, O Kulasundara, that one will certainly arrest the semen. With this mantra, the wise man should effect the arrest of semen. (9) [The Method for Arresting Semen]

Listen to that which was taught for the destruction of laziness: having summoned the sound of the syllable *huṃ* and clapping both hands twice, the wise man should grind the root of a *vetāla* tree and consume it. Then, having consecrated the root of a palmyra palm with the utterance of *phaṭ*, the wise man should drink it. Thereafter...

The wise man should drink honey; it shall be the destroyer of laziness. O Ānandabhairava, listen as I describe the destruction of sleep: having mixed half a *tolaka* of lac with half a *tolaka* of mustard oil and white incense, [one should use] the mantra.

The wise one should recite this mantra; I shall declare that mantra by which the destruction of sleep occurs. O Goddess! Sleep is indeed equal to Yama; sleep is considered the cause of disease. Through sleep, every fault arises, and through sleep, knowledge is destroyed. By means of sleep, everything dissolves away.

Through sleep one goes to hell; therefore, O Bhairava, one should strive with effort to destroy sleep. Having extracted the three [syllables] in sequence—*sambarta* joined with *vahni* (fire) and combined with the crescent moon (*candrakhaṇḍa*)—one should utter *vahnijāyā* (the wife of fire, *svāhā*) at the end. [Recite this] one hundred and eight times.

Having recited [the mantra], one should rub [the eyes] with great effort; by applying this daily to the eyes, it is said that sleep is destroyed. Then, one should recite the Vāgbhava [mantra] over the central parts of both eyes. Thereafter, one should diligently meditate upon the family preceptor (kulaguru) and the family goddess (kuladevī).
One should pray with great effort for the swift destruction of sleep:
"Oṃ! O Goddess Sleep! O Mahāmāyā! O Cause of the world’s liberation! Destroy me, O Mother of the World! Destroy me, O Supreme Sovereign! Having first uttered the *praṇava* (Oṃ).

Then one should utter the *nidrā-pati-pada* (the word for the lord of sleep); thereafter, one should utter the *sanātanī* (the eternal one). Then one should utter the *vahnijāyā* (the wife of fire, i.e., *svāhā*). This is considered the mantra for the destruction of sleep. By the mere recitation (*japa*) of this mantra, the destruction of sleep will certainly occur—whether one hundred and eight times or even a thousand times.

O Kuleśvara! By reciting [the mantra], sleep comes to an end; what else shall I tell you? Here, by supplying the ellipsis (*adhyāhāra*) from the word "sthitvā" (having stayed), there is a single agent for the action expressed by "japtvā" (having recited). 11.
Now I shall further explain the restraint of the senses according to the path taught in the *Yonitantra*.
For he fashions the form of the family. O Lord! Having brought a lovely and charming woman with great effort, one should conquer her by that path and desire her with great effort.
By means of this practice of honoring [the deity], men shall achieve the retention of semen (*śukrastambha*). Whosoever possesses the state of being one with their chosen deity...

Having meditated upon the entire world as being of the same form as the deity who is remembered, one should drink the wine. Then, through the practice of breath control (prāṇāyāma), one should bring the vital air under control.
Thereafter, O Śiva, having stirred the ghee and likewise ground the root of the *nāla* plant, [one should proceed].

Having recited the previously mentioned mantra, the practitioner should drink it; at that very moment, the man becomes liberated from all diseases. O Mahādeva! Having meditated upon the dust of the Guru’s feet, [he should drink it] combined with honey and meat, and joined with wine.

One should rub it with great effort; then, having consecrated it with the previously mentioned mantra, one should drink it for eight days. By means of this method of purification, the destruction of thirst will certainly occur. (3)
Then, having meditated upon Kuleśvarī, who is dark and variegated, one should thereafter drink [the substance].
Then, O Kālabhairava, one should drink liquor, meat, or ghee. By means of this application of consecration, the destruction of hunger certainly occurs.
This speech is fashioned from the wish-fulfilling gem, exceedingly vast and endowed with all virtues;
it is like a manifest kalpa-tree, providing for all needs and beneficial for the welfare of the entire world.
Having meditated upon this *Śrī-Prāṇatoṣiṇī*, which is honored by the wise and yields abundant fruit.
O wise and virtuous one, you should behold this most radiant creeper.
Thus ends the Śrī Prāṇatoṣiṇī.
